info.name: OpenCred Server (Docker)
info.description:
HTTP requests for the OpenCred Docker image (`apps/server`). Targets the `/v1/*` API surface.

## How to use

1. Start the container locally (or via SSH tunnel if it's on a remote VM):
   ```
   docker run -d --name opencred -p 3100:3100 \
     -e OPENCRED_API_KEY="$OPENCRED_API_KEY" \
     -e OPENCRED_KEY_PATH=/secrets/issuer-key.pem \
     -v $PWD/keys/issuer-key.pem:/secrets/issuer-key.pem:ro \
     opencred:bootcamp
   ```
2. In Postman, edit the collection variables (Variables tab):
   - `baseUrl` — default `http://localhost:3100`
   - `apiKey` — paste the value of `OPENCRED_API_KEY`
3. Run **Public → GET /v1/health** to confirm `signingKeyLoaded: true`.
4. Run **Inspect → GET /v1/keys** — it auto-saves `issuerDid` into the collection variables for the issue requests.
5. Run **Issue & Verify → POST /v1/credentials/issue (vc-jwt)** — it auto-saves the response into `lastCredential` for the verify request.
6. Run **Issue & Verify → POST /v1/credentials/verify**.

Authentication is set at the collection level (Bearer `{{apiKey}}`); the two public endpoints override to no auth.

request.description:
Issue a credential with a compact JWT proof — the server's default. Works with every bundled schema (no JSON-LD context strict-mode constraints).

The response `credential` is a JSON-LD VC object whose `proof.jwt` holds the compact JWS.

Auto-saves the response into `{{lastCredential}}` for the verify request.

Issue a JSON-LD VC with a Data Integrity proof. Requires an EC key on the server side (RSA returns 500 CRYPTO_ERROR) and a JSON-LD context that does not redefine W3C-protected terms (otherwise 500 CRYPTO_ERROR: Invalid JSON-LD syntax). Prefer `vc-jwt` for portable workshops.
Issue an SD-JWT VC. The `~`-separated compact token contains hashes of the disclosable claims plus the disclosures themselves. The holder can choose which to reveal.

Issue a credential against a JSON Schema you paste in the request body — no need for the schema to be in the bundled registry. The server compiles the schema, validates `credentialSubject` against it, and writes the schema's `$id` (or a base64 data-URI fallback) into the credential's `credentialSchema` block.

When `inlineSchema` is provided, `schemaId` becomes optional. If both are passed, the inline schema wins for validation and `credentialSchema.id`.

When `revocationRegistryUrl` is set, the server attaches a `credentialStatus` block of type `dedi` and generates a `urn:uuid:` credential id. The hash is computed automatically. Use the Revocation requests to publish/query status.

One-call issue + package. The same `customization` knobs documented on `/v1/credentials/package` apply here. The response shape:

```json
{
  "credential": { ... },
  "proofFormat": "vc-jwt",
  "isCompactToken": false,
  "packagedOutputs": [
    { "format": "qr-png", "data": "data:image/png;base64,...", "encoding": "utf-8" },
    { "format": "qr-svg", "data": "<svg ...>", "encoding": "utf-8" },
    { "format": "pdf",    "data": "JVBERi0...", "encoding": "base64" },
    { "format": "json",   "data": "{ ... }", "encoding": "utf-8" }
  ]
}
```

Works with `proofFormat: "data-integrity"` and `"sd-jwt-vc"` too — for sd-jwt-vc the QR embeds the raw compact token verbatim.

exec: // Build the verify body programmatically from {{lastCredential}}.
// Why a pre-request script: the issue endpoint returns `credential`
// as either a string (vc-jwt, sd-jwt-vc) or an object (data-integrity).
// The post-response scripts on the issue requests JSON.stringify the
// object form, so {{lastCredential}} is always a string. But naive
// the JSON-stringified object contains literal `"` characters which
// terminate the surrounding string early and produce malformed JSON
// (the server returns 400 INVALID_JSON in that case).
// JSON.stringify on the value handles both forms uniformly — it
// produces a properly-escaped JSON string literal for embedding.
console.warn('lastCredential is empty — run an issue request first.');
const body = JSON.stringify({ credential: stored ?? '' }, null, 2);

request.description:
Verify any of the three proof formats — the server auto-detects. The `credential` field is a string: a JSON-stringified VC for data-integrity, or the compact token for vc-jwt and sd-jwt-vc.

The body is built programmatically by a **pre-request script** that reads `{{lastCredential}}` and JSON-encodes it safely. This works whether the credential came from `data-integrity` (object → stringified, contains `"`), `vc-jwt`, or `sd-jwt-vc`. The literal `"raw"` shown in Postman's body editor is overwritten before the request is sent — it's only there for documentation.

`{{lastCredential}}` is set by the issue requests above.

Publish a DID document (public keys + verification methods) to the DeDi `public_key_registry` so verifiers can resolve the issuer's keys without a separate DID registrar.

The same `rejectKeyMaterial` defense-in-depth guard runs on the body — a `privateKey` field, or any string starting with `-----BEGIN ... PRIVATE KEY-----`, fails 400 before anything reaches DeDi.

Returns `503 DEDI_NOT_CONFIGURED` until `OPENCRED_DEDI_*` env vars are set.

Resolve a DID document from the DeDi `public_key_registry`. POST (not GET) so DIDs containing colons or slashes don't have to be URL-encoded.

Returns `{ did, document?, keyStatus }`. `document` is omitted for `did:key` records (the verifier derives it from the DID itself); `keyStatus` is `"current"` or `"rotated"`. The response may also include a `proof` block (CORD-blockchain anchor metadata) when DeDi anchored the record on-chain.

503 if DeDi isn't configured.

Idempotently bootstrap a DeDi namespace and the four registries OpenCred needs (`vc-revocation-registry`, `public_key_registry`, `schema_registry`, `context_registry`).

Wraps the same `dediClient.ensureRegistries(...)` helper that runs once at server startup, so you can spin up additional namespaces at runtime without restarting the container — useful for per-tenant setups.

Replace `your-namespace-id` in the body with the namespace ID issued by your DeDi operator. Unverified namespaces look like `did:web:did.cord.network:xyz`; verified ones look like `xyz.org`.

Returns `{ namespace, registries }` listing the registry names that now exist on the namespace (whether freshly created or already present).

Returns `503 DEDI_NOT_CONFIGURED` until `OPENCRED_DEDI_*` env vars are set. The same `rejectKeyMaterial` defense-in-depth guard runs on the body.

Compute the JCS+SHA-256 revocation hash for a credential. Works **without** DeDi configured — pure hash computation. The hash is what gets published to a revocation registry.

Auto-saves the hash into `{{lastRevocationHash}}` for the revoke/status requests.
Compute hashes for many credentials at once. Returns `revocationHashes[]` keyed by `credentialId` (or a positional `index:N` token if a credential has no `id`).

Publish the hash to DeDi as revoked. Returns 503 DEDI_NOT_CONFIGURED unless `OPENCRED_DEDI_BASE_URL` (and friends) are set on the server.

You can also send `{ "credential": {...} }` and the server will hash it for you. Add `"namespace": "..."` to override the configured default.

`reason` is an optional free-text descriptor (per the DeDi canonical revoke.json schema) — typical values are short tags like `"key-compromised"`, `"superseded"`, or `"holder-request"`. When supplied, it is stored on the DeDi record and echoed by `/v1/credentials/revocation-status`.
Query DeDi for the current status of a hash. Same 503 if DeDi isn't wired up.

request.description:
Render packaged outputs for a signed credential.

## What you get back

`outputs[]` always has one entry per requested `format`. Each entry has:

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| `format` | `qr-png` / `qr-svg` / `pdf` / `json` |
| `mimeType` | `image/png`, `image/svg+xml`, `application/pdf`, `application/json` |
| `suggestedFileName` | Slugged from credential `type` + last 8 chars of `id` |
| `encoding` | `base64` for PDF; `utf-8` for everything else |
| `data` | The actual content (string) |

**Decoding gotcha:** `qr-png` returns a `data:image/png;base64,<...>` URL string with `encoding: "utf-8"` (the base64 is *inside* the URL). The PDF returns pure base64 with `encoding: "base64"`. So:

```bash
# qr-png — strip the data-URL prefix first:
jq -r '.outputs[] | select(.format=="qr-png") | .data | sub("^data:image/png;base64,"; "")' resp.json | base64 -d > qr.png

# pdf — straight base64:
jq -r '.outputs[] | select(.format=="pdf")    | .data' resp.json | base64 -d > cert.pdf

# qr-svg / json — already utf-8:
jq -r '.outputs[] | select(.format=="qr-svg") | .data' resp.json > qr.svg
jq -r '.outputs[] | select(.format=="json")   | .data' resp.json > credential.json
```

## Input — works with all three proof formats

- `data-integrity` and `vc-jwt` → `credential` is a JSON-LD VC object (object literal in the body).
- `sd-jwt-vc` → `credential` is a compact `~`-separated token string (just paste the string).

For compact-token input, the server decodes the JWT payload offline (no signature check — packaging is a rendering step) to drive the PDF certificate layout, and embeds the original token verbatim in the QR code so any verifier scanning it runs a real cryptographic check.

## Customization

All fields under `customization` are optional. Common ones: `primaryColor` (hex), `issuerDisplayName` (NOT `issuerName` — that gets silently dropped), `secondaryColor`, `textColor`, `labelColor`, `backgroundColor`, `logoDataUri` (data: URI), `sealDataUri`, `footerText` (pass `""` to suppress the verification disclaimer).

A pre-request script reads `{{lastCredential}}` and sends it as either an object or a string depending on what the issue endpoint returned — no manual juggling. The static `raw` body shown here is the fallback for when you haven't run an issue request yet.

Kick off a batch issuance from CSV content. The first row is the header; subsequent rows become credentials. Returns a `jobId` you poll with the next two requests.

Capped by `OPENCRED_BATCH_ROW_LIMIT` (default 1000).
Poll batch progress: `pending` / `running` / `completed` / `failed`, plus row counts.
Once the job is `completed`, fetch the per-row signed credentials and any errors.
